respStmt.note: Incorporation of index card for parish church of St Sepulchre (Holborn)

provenance.orgName: London. Parish church of St Sepulchre (Holborn)
provenance.p: An index card in Neil R. Ker's handwriting assigns this manuscript to the parish church of St Sepulchre. It was likewise listed under this parish church in the Supplement, p. 73. However, based on the same provenance evidence (described more fully below), the editors of MLGB3 assigned the manuscript instead to the Augustinian priory of St Bartholomew. Ker particularly noted that St Sepulchre belonged to St Bartholomew, and was partially rebuilt at the cost of Sir John Popham (named in the manuscript; see further below). Ker cites E. A. Webb, The records of St. Bartholomew's priory and of the church and parish of St. Bartholomew the Great, West Smithfield, p. 366.

provenance.orgName: London. Augustinian priory of St Bartholomew, Smithfield
provenance.p: On fol. 2v an inscription of s. xv: 'Orate pro animabus m. Johannis Lorde et Ursule uxoris eius Simonis Briggeman Marione uxoris eius et omnium benefactorum eorundem cum quorum bonis iste liber comparatus fuit et datus hanc ecclesie per media Willemi Taylard' (inscription repeated on 119v).

That the priory of St Bartholomew the Great was intended by 'haec ecclesia' is proved by two added lists of benefactors to the priory, including the known patron Sir John Popham (c. 1395–1463) and two priors of St. Bartholomew's, Reynold (Reginald) Collier (d. 1471) and Richard Pulter (d. 1480) (fol. 120v). Among the benefactors named on fol. 121r are 'Walteri Taylard pro edificacione capelle' and 'm. Johannis Lord pro hoc processionale'.

The manuscript had formerly been owned by Thomas Woodstock (1355–1397), duke of Gloucester, son of Edward III: inscription on fol. 2r (almost completely effaced), '. . . est de la chapelle Thomas fitz au Roy, Duc de Gloucr achete de Sr Henry Wynchestre'. The chapel would have been his personal chapel rather than his collegiate church at Pleshey castle since this book must have been among those confiscated at his attainder and subsequently sold, to have passed to St Bartholomew's not very much later.

history.provenance: Confiscated and sold after Woodstock's attainder for treason. Acquired by William Taylard and friends for presentation to the Augustinian priory of St Bartholomew the Great, London, Smithfield.
Inscriptions: 'Chambirleyne' (fol. 1v, s. xv ex); 'Thomas Brudenell' (fol. 1r, s. xvi in).
Cest livre est a [...]ri [......] apres par remaner a droitz hier [...] du dit henr' pur toutz iours (fol. 121 at foot, partly erased).
Robert Harley (1661–1724), 1st earl of Oxford and Mortimer, politician.
Edward Harley (1689–1741), 2nd earl of Oxford and Mortimer, book collector and patron of the arts.
Henrietta Cavendish Harley (1694–1755), countess of Oxford and Mortimer, née Holles, patron of architecture.
Margaret Cavendish Bentinck (1715–1785), duchess of Portland, née Harley, patron of arts and sciences, by whom with her mother the Harleian library was sold to the nation in 1753.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Record updated by Sian Witherden to reflect an earlier decision assigning the parish church of St Sepulchre (Holborn), informed by the corresponding card in Neil R. Ker, et al., ‘Medieval Libraries of Great Britain’, index, Oxford, 1937–2025 (held at Oxford, Bodleian Library). Provenance evidence certainty level for St Sepulchre adjusted to low. French ownership inscription also added from index card.
